MEDIA AND WORDPRESS MENUS List/search media first; results are paginated. Reuse existing attachments. upload-media accepts exactly one of sourceUrl or base64; it reads nothing from the server's disk. Base64 requires a filename and is limited to 512 KB decoded. Provide meaningful alt text for images. Use returned IDs/URLs in the actual target block's schema; different core/ACF blocks have different image attribute formats. SVG is not accepted: it is markup that can carry scripts. Ask the site admin to add one in the media library.
delete-media is PERMANENT by default. Referenced files can still be deleted. usedBy reports detected references; it is not a blocking check or a complete dependency graph. Deleting a WPML original may affect its language copies; check the multilingual contract. Repoint known usages when replacing an image, and do not delete outside the user's requested scope.
List menus before create-menu; use returned menu IDs with update-menu or delete-menu. update-menu items replaces the WHOLE tree, including children. Read, modify and resend the whole tree; omit items to rename only. Follow the schema for one link target per item (url/postId/termId/archive). Use real IDs and safe URLs. Keep attached object links attached rather than converting them to guessed URLs. A classic WordPress menu does not automatically appear in a core/navigation block. Inspect the actual navigation block and its references/content. Theme menu locations and Gutenberg navigation content are different systems; do not invent a menu attribute for core or ACF blocks. A menu is visible only when an existing theme/block uses it. Verify its real frontend location. A core/navigation block carries its own links as inner blocks, written as comments only (no HTML): <!-- wp:navigation {"overlayMenu":"mobile","ariaLabel":"Main"} --> <!-- wp:navigation-link {"label":"Visit us","type":"page","id":<pageId>,"url":"<its address>","kind":"post-type"} /--> <!-- wp:navigation-link {"label":"Shop","url":"https://example.com/","kind":"custom"} /--> <!-- /wp:navigation --> A link to a page keeps its id and address together; a submenu is wp:navigation-submenu with links inside.
Forms have their own rules: get-skill-doc {id:"forms-contract"}.
